Management summary

Months across, each line as a value and as a percentage of sales. This is the layout that becomes the standard client pack.

Profit & loss

Month and year to date against the same period last year, with the variance in value and percent.

Balance sheet

At the month end selected, against the same month last year. Prior year results sit unposted while the audit is open — line B-640 — which is what makes the statement balance.

Actual against budget

Month and year to date against budget, with the variance in value and percent, and the full-year outturn as actual to date plus budget for the months remaining.

All bank and cash accounts together.

Sales analysis

Where the sales came from, who they were made to, and how that has changed. Net sales are taken from the revenue accounts in the ledger; the customer analysis is built from the sales journals posted to each customer account, so it is the invoiced value including VAT — the two are shown side by side rather than mixed.

Sales by month

The ten largest customers

Invoiced in the period, including VAT.

By customer

Month by month

Account movements

Every nominal account in the ledger, what it moved in the period, and the report line it is mapped to. This is the bridge between the client's own chart of accounts and the statements — and it is where an account that has been left unmapped, or mapped to the wrong line, shows itself.

Statements

A single customer or supplier account, every movement on it, with the balance carried down. This is the statement that goes to the client or to the supplier, so it reads from the ledger and nothing else.

Transactions

The whole journal, searchable. Every posting the app holds for this client, exactly as BTMS wrote it — the audit trail behind every figure in every report.

Account mapping

How each account in the client's own chart of accounts is treated in the statements — set once per client. This is the only thing that differs between one client and the next: the reports, the checks and the audit are identical.

What a change here doesChanging a mapping moves that account onto a different line of the profit and loss or the balance sheet from the next report run. It never touches BTMS and it never re-writes a posting — the ledger is the book of record. A change is recorded against the user who made it.

Company setup

The client's own particulars. These appear on every printed report and statement, and they are what the audit file and the statutory deadlines are driven from.

Held against this clientEverything on this page belongs to this client alone and travels with the client record, not with the app.

Stock

The BTMS stock valuation at each date it was run, against the stock account in the ledger. The two do not agree at any of the four dates, and the gap changes sign — which is the first thing to settle before a gross margin is reported to this client.

Why it mattersCost of sales is driven by the stock movement. A valuation that does not tie to the ledger means the gross margin on the P&L is not the margin the business actually made — and the negative quantities point at goods issued before they were received, or receipts never posted.

Debtors and creditors

Ageing at 31 July 2026, applied oldest-first because the BTMS export carries no allocation between receipts and invoices. Both tables tie to the trial balance to the cent.

Debtors ageing

Where the money owed actually sits.

Creditors ageing

What the business owes, by age.

How the ledger has moved

The balance at each month end, the part of it older than ninety days, and the opposite-sign balances sitting inside it. Every month in the ledger is rebuilt, so a month that was never reviewed still appears here.

Accounts to look at

Flagged on four tests: money older than ninety days, a balance on the wrong side, a balance that grew on the month, and no movement for ninety days on an account that still carries a balance.

Every account

VAT

Every posting that carries a BTMS VAT code is rebuilt into the return boxes from the journal itself — output tax from the sales journals, input tax from the purchase journals, with the notional output leg on the reverse-charge codes raised automatically. Where a filed return has been attached, the two are set against each other box by box.

Returns held

Every quarter the ledger covers, and whether the return actually submitted has been attached to it. A quarter with no return attached is computed but untested.

The return boxes

Computed from the ledger, against the return as filed. A variance of more than one cent is flagged.

By VAT code

Where a variance sits. The base is the net amount the code was applied to; the tax is what BTMS calculated on it.

Every quarter in the ledger

Needs attention

What the checks found across all 84.725 postings. Nothing here has been sent to the client — this is the list that gets worked before a pack is issued.

Audit file

The same ledger, examined the way a file is examined rather than the way a month is reviewed: materiality set, analytical review, journal entry testing, items above the threshold listed for vouching, cut-off tested, and every test recorded with its result.

Materiality

Analytical review

Journal entry testing

Every posting carries the journal that raised it. Manual journals are the ones that matter — they are the only entries a person composes freely.

Items above performance materiality

Cut-off

Monthly audit review — working papers

The monthly programme. Each step is a working paper: it carries its result, who prepared it, who reviewed it, and the date each signed. A month cannot be closed while a step is unsigned or an exception stands.

Sign-offs on this draft are held in your own browser. In the built application they sit in the database with the user who signed, the time they signed, and a locked period once the month is closed.

Test log

The evidence behind the programme — what each test showed across the whole ledger.

Data import

What has been loaded from BTMS for this client, and when. Every feed is imported inside the app with the client already chosen — the BTMS ledger, trial balance, stock valuation and chart of accounts carry no client name in the file, so the file is fingerprinted against this client's own account codes before a single row is accepted.

Working ledger

What the app is reading from at this moment.

Import checklist

A tick is a month that has been loaded. A dash is a month that is due and has not been. A dot is a month not yet reached. The annual trial balance is asked for once a year, and not at all once every closed month has a monthly one.

Reconciliation

Two independent proofs: the journal must balance on its own, and it must agree to the trial balance BTMS produced for the same period.

Client setup

One application, configured per client. These switches decide which of the sections above appear and what each of them contains — nothing here is a separate build.

How a new client is addedImport their chart of accounts, accept or adjust the suggested mapping onto the master report lines, set the switches below, import a month, and check it against their trial balance. No code, no new report.
